site.source: shared/sites.ts, from NASA Lunar Surface Data Book (M2M-30044) table A2.1-1. Center of an original candidate-region polygon; not an approved landing site.

nature: Terrain visualization of LOLA-derived topography. Lighting in the .blend is illustrative. Not a guarantee of power, communications, visibility or landing suitability.

source.product: NASA GSFC PGDA product 78, adjusted local LOLA 5 m/pixel elevation (Site06 = Nobile rim 1)
source.frame: MOON_ME reference frame of ephemeris DE421 (stated by the provider README; not encoded in the GeoTIFF CRS)
source.valueMeaning: Surface height Z in meters above a 1,737,400 m reference sphere; interpolation fills pixels without LOLA returns
source.citation: Barker et al. (2021), Planetary and Space Science 203, 105119, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119
source.pixelRegistration: Values at pixel centers (GMT pixel registration, AREA_OR_POINT=Area); centers at edge + 2.5 m
source.license: NASA data; redistribution/publication review remains a project release gate.

crs.projection: Polar stereographic, south pole origin (lat_0=-90), central meridian 0, scale 1 at the pole, false easting/northing 0
crs.frame: MOON_ME reference frame of ephemeris DE421 (stated by the provider README; not encoded in the GeoTIFF CRS)
crs.frameCaveat: MOON_ME (DE421) and MOON_PA differ by about 875 m on the surface; do not mix frames.

verticalReference: Height above the 1,737,400 m reference sphere (radius = height + 1,737,400 m); not a geoid.

localOrigin.rule: Site projected X/Y and source bilinear elevation rounded to whole meters

axes.blender: Z-up, right-handed: X = projected X - origin X, Y = projected Y - origin Y, Z = height - origin height
axes.glb: glTF Y-up, right-handed: x = projected X - origin X, y = height - origin height, z = -(projected Y - origin Y)
axes.gridNorthNote: Projected +Y is grid north (toward 0° E away from the pole), not geographic north.
axes.azimuthToGridBearing: gridBearing = geographicAzimuth + longitudeEastDeg (local, clockwise from projected +Y); varies by about ±3° across the crop

steps: rho = 2 * R * tan(pi/4 + latRad/2) with R = 1737400 (latRad negative)
X = rho * sin(lonEastRad); Y = rho * cos(lonEastRad)
h: source raster height (bilinear) or the GLB surface height at (X, Y) plus a marker offset
inverse: X = gltf.x + origin.projectedXM; Y = origin.projectedYM - gltf.z; h = gltf.y + origin.elevationM
lonEast = atan2(X, Y); lat = -(pi/2 - 2 * atan(hypot(X, Y) / (2R)))

geographicEnvelope.note: Envelope of the projected square; the square itself is the coverage, not this lat/lon box.

coverage.insideTest: A coordinate is covered when its projected X/Y lies inside meshExtentProjectedM (a square in projected meters, not a lat/lon box).
coverage.gapPolicy: A 25 m quad is omitted if any source pixel in its footprint is missing; none were missing in this crop.
coverage.interpolationNote: The provider fills pixels without LOLA returns by interpolation (about 90% of pixels in the studied polar 5 m grids per PGDA product 78). Valid elevation does not mean direct measurement.

mesh.vertexSampling: Exact source values at every step-th source pixel center (no averaging)
mesh.triangulation: Each quad split along the diagonal from its north-west vertex to its south-east vertex (grid axes)
mesh.geometryModel: 2.5D height field on the projected plane: horizontal distances are grid distances (true ground distance ≈ grid / 1.001587 at the site); lunar curvature is not applied (sphere drop about 7.2 m at 5 km).

objects: Marker_<site> and Marker_ridge-reference (empties at exact points; poles start 10 m above)
Camera_ground_to_ridge (site, 2 m above the mesh, aimed at the ridge reference)

reproduction: See README.md in the site-terrain directory.
